description: Not mechanically checkable. Loaded ONLY by the reviewer agent, never by the build thread.

S1.name: Blocker
S1.definition: User cannot make the decision, is likely to make a wrong one, an accessibility gate fails, or a destructive action is unsafely presented.

S2.name: Major
S2.definition: Decision is possible but materially slower or error-prone.

S3.name: Minor
S3.definition: Adds friction or inconsistency without threatening the decision.

S4.name: Polish
S4.definition: Craft refinement with no functional impact.

rules.name: No redundant low-tier encoding
rules.check: P2 and P3 elements use at most 2 emphasis devices.
rules.fix: Pick one device: border or tint or bold, not all three.

rules.name: Motion reserved for alerts
rules.check: Motion is applied only to state changes requiring human intervention.
rules.fix: Remove decorative animation and entrance effects.

rules.name: Links for navigation
rules.check: Controls that change context without performing an operation render as links.
rules.fix: Convert navigation buttons to links.

rules.name: No homeless actions
rules.check: Every action belongs to a scope present on the surface.
rules.fix: Remove or relocate actions that belong elsewhere.

rules.name: Adjacent-rank pairing
rules.check: Side-by-side actions differ by 1 to 3 ranks on the emphasis ladder.
rules.fix: Adjust treatments so paired actions are neither equal nor extremely distant.

rules.name: Placement by container
rules.check: Primary placement follows the container convention table.
rules.fix: Move the primary to the conventional position for its container.

rules.name: Order by workflow then frequency
rules.check: Action order follows workflow sequence, else descending frequency. Never alphabetical.
rules.fix: Reorder.

rules.name: Optimistic versus pessimistic
rules.check: Irreversible actions never show optimistic success.
rules.fix: Use pending state and server confirmation for irreversible actions.

rules.name: Toggles are state, flows get setup affordances
rules.check: On/off toggles appear only on actions that take complete effect on flip; configuration flows render as a setup affordance with the action label and current status.
rules.fix: Replace the toggle with a setup card or button (Configure, Verify) plus status; reserve toggles for immediately effective boolean state.

rules.name: Confirmation content
rules.check: Confirmations name the object, state the effect and cascade, state reversibility, and use action-restating labels.
rules.fix: Rewrite the confirmation; replace Yes and No with explicit action labels.

rules.name: Identity first
rules.check: Lists, tables, and cards lead with the human-recognizable identity attribute.
rules.fix: Move the identity attribute to the first and most prominent position.

rules.name: State always visible
rules.check: Objects with a lifecycle display their state consistently everywhere.
rules.fix: Add a consistent state indicator.

rules.name: Glance test
rules.check: Elements in a zone would be read within one 3-second glance to answer one question.
rules.fix: Split zones whose elements serve different glances.

rules.name: Move test
rules.check: Moving an element between zones changes the meaning of both.
rules.fix: Merge or redefine arbitrary zones.

rules.name: Card sort simulation
rules.check: The grouping is independently re-derivable from the element list.
rules.fix: Try alternative organizing axes and compare.

rules.name: Maximum 7 nav items per group
rules.check: Each navigation group holds 7 or fewer items.
rules.fix: Introduce labeled groups rather than scrolling.

rules.name: Never mix nav layers
rules.check: Global, section, contextual, and detail layers use distinct controls.
rules.fix: Separate filters from navigation and areas from views.

rules.name: Path back preserves state
rules.check: Return navigation restores filters, sort, and scroll position.
rules.fix: Persist view state across navigation.

rules.name: Dashboard is not the app
rules.check: Full workflows live in their own area and are linked, not embedded.
rules.fix: Link out rather than embedding a workflow.

rules.name: Disclosure is not navigation
rules.check: In-place expansion is used for detail; context changes use navigation.
rules.fix: Convert misused accordions to navigation, and the reverse.

rules.name: Filter scope visible
rules.check: Global filters sit above all content; local filters are visually contained by their zone.
rules.fix: Attach filters to the region they affect.

rules.name: Three to five global filters
rules.check: Default view shows at most 5 global filters; the rest sit behind a More filters affordance with an active count.
rules.fix: Move surplus filters behind a disclosure with a count badge.

rules.name: Active filters shown as content
rules.check: Applied filters render as removable chips with a Clear all action.
rules.fix: Add filter chips and a clear-all control.

rules.name: Deliberate defaults
rules.check: Default filter state answers the top-ranked question for the most common user.
rules.fix: Replace all-time or all-segment defaults with a meaningful default.

rules.name: State in the URL
rules.check: Filter, sort, and view state is encoded in the URL.
rules.fix: Serialize view state to the URL for shareability.

rules.name: Label consistency
rules.check: One concept uses one word across the product.
rules.fix: Standardize terminology.

rules.name: Significance threshold
rules.check: Deltas below a defined threshold render neutral.
rules.fix: Define and apply a significance threshold.

rules.name: Direction is not goodness
rules.check: Color encodes favorability, not the sign of the delta.
rules.fix: Bind color to whether the movement is good for this metric.

rules.name: Tables are underrated
rules.check: Which-ones questions are answered by a sorted table, not a chart.
rules.fix: Replace with a table and a deliberate default sort.

rules.name: Legend adjacency
rules.check: Legends sit adjacent to their data, or series are labeled directly.
rules.fix: Move or replace the legend with direct labels.

rules.name: Module size from tier
rules.check: Module span follows the tier span map.
rules.fix: Resize modules to match tiers.

rules.name: Real drill paths
rules.check: Drill hierarchies match the user mental model.
rules.fix: Replace invented hierarchies with real ones.

rules.name: Trend words require trend data
rules.check: No rendered or assistive copy states a direction for a metric unless a series is supplied; point-in-time values render as values or endpoint deltas, never as narrated trends.
rules.fix: Show the supplied endpoints or delta and delete the direction word; chart a trend only from a supplied series.

rules.name: Visible cross-filtering
rules.check: Cross-filter effects are immediately obvious and reversible in one action.
rules.fix: Add an explicit applied-filter indicator and a clear control.

rules.name: Context preserved on drill
rules.check: Drill-down keeps parent context and restores prior state on return.
rules.fix: Add breadcrumb and state restoration.

rules.name: Tooltips carry precision only
rules.check: No information required for a top-ranked question is hover-only.
rules.fix: Surface required information; keep tooltips for exact values and definitions.

rules.name: Errors are actionable
rules.check: Error states say what failed, whether it is retryable, and the remedy. No raw codes alone.
rules.fix: Rewrite error content with cause and remedy.

rules.name: System before view
rules.check: No styling values are defined at the view level.
rules.fix: Promote one-off values into tokens or components.

rules.name: Declared grid
rules.check: A 12-column grid with defined gutter and max width is declared and followed.
rules.fix: Express module widths in columns.

rules.name: Component from question
rules.check: Component choice follows the selection tables.
rules.fix: Replace with the component matching the situation.

rules.name: No nested overlays
rules.check: No modal opens another modal.
rules.fix: Decompose into a page or a multi-step flow.

rules.name: Presets before pickers
rules.check: Date range controls offer presets before a calendar.
rules.fix: Add presets and order them first.

rules.name: Native controls wear the theme
rules.check: Every native form control that renders — select, input, textarea, checkbox, radio, button — carries the surface's ground, ink, border, and focus tokens; a control that shows the user agent's default white box, default border, or default text color on a themed ground is a render defect, and a select whose current value is not legible is an unset-state defect.
rules.fix: Style each native control family with the surface tokens (background, color, border, accent-color, focus ring) and verify by screenshot on the surface's actual ground.

rules.name: Keyboard complete
rules.check: All actions are keyboard reachable and operable in logical order with no traps.
rules.fix: Fix tab order and add keyboard handlers.

rules.name: Live regions
rules.check: Async updates, load completion, and errors are announced.
rules.fix: Add live region announcements.

rules.name: Chart alternatives
rules.check: Every chart has an accessible equivalent: data table, summary sentence, or both.
rules.fix: Add a text summary and an accessible data table.

rules.name: Purpose before styling
rules.check: Purpose and structure passes complete before styling critique.
rules.fix: Return to pass 1.

rules.name: Severity on every finding
rules.check: Every finding carries a severity and a rule ID.
rules.fix: Add severities and rule IDs.

rules.name: Gate thresholds
rules.check: Ship requires score of at least 112 of 140, zero S1, at most 2 S2, and D1, D2, D3, D7 each at least 3.
rules.fix: Fix blocking findings before shipping.

rules.name: Remove and justify
rules.check: Every element survives the removal test with a concrete answer.
rules.fix: Remove or demote elements that fail.

rules.name: Subtraction pass
rules.check: A pass permitting only removal was performed before finalizing.
rules.fix: Perform the subtraction pass.

rules.name: Alternative artifact test
rules.check: Considered whether an alert, report, or workflow change serves better than a dashboard.
rules.fix: Propose the better artifact.

rules.name: Name what is working
rules.check: The critique report includes a what-is-working section.
rules.fix: Add it to prevent regression.

rules.name: Fix the earliest link
rules.check: Findings are fixed in Spine order.
rules.fix: Reorder the fix list by stage.

rules.name: One structural change per iteration
rules.check: Structural changes are made one at a time.
rules.fix: Split the iteration.

rules.name: Re-run after structural change
rules.check: Passes 2 through 8 re-run after any structural change.
rules.fix: Re-run the protocol.

rules.name: Stop condition
rules.check: Stop when the gate passes and remaining findings are S3 or S4 with low value-to-effort.
rules.fix: Document the remainder and stop.

rules.name: Adversarial framing
rules.check: Self-critique is run in a find-the-failures posture.
rules.fix: Re-run the critique adversarially.

rules.name: Separate authoring from review
rules.check: Critique is a distinct step with the rule catalog reloaded.
rules.fix: Re-run critique without reference to authoring rationale.

rules.name: Quota critique
rules.check: First review produces at least 5 findings including at least 1 at S2 or higher.
rules.fix: Examine states, extremes, accessibility, and content.

rules.name: Steelman the alternative
rules.check: The strongest case for the rejected option is stated.
rules.fix: Write the steelman.

rules.name: No code before the gate
rules.check: Implementation code is not emitted until A9 passes.
rules.fix: Produce the artifact chain first.

rules.name: Artifact IDs in code
rules.check: Components reference their element and action IDs.
rules.fix: Annotate components with IDs and tiers.

rules.name: Artifacts must be produced
rules.check: The artifact chain exists, not merely the knowledge of it.
rules.fix: Produce the artifacts.

rules.name: Single primary commitment
rules.check: The surface carries one primary commitment; secondary paths are subordinate in contrast, area, or placement.
rules.fix: Demote every competing call to action and keep one label, destination, and promise.

rules.name: Claim-proof adjacency
rules.check: Every meaningful claim carries its evidence in the same viewport, module, or reading beat.
rules.fix: Move the evidence beside the claim, or drop the claim.

rules.name: Evidence is real and attributable
rules.check: Every metric, quote, customer, logo, certification, award, and urgency signal is real, attributable, and within the permission granted.
rules.fix: Remove invented proof and replace it with an honest operating fact or a direct demonstration.

rules.name: First viewport orients
rules.check: Without scrolling the visitor can name what this is, the sharpest promise, one adjacent reason to believe, and the next step.
rules.fix: Rebuild the first viewport around those four answers and move feature grids and FAQ below it.

rules.name: Objections ordered by decision cost
rules.check: Objections are resolved in the order they block progress, and no purchase-blocking objection sits in an FAQ or footer.
rules.fix: Rank objections by prevalence, severity, and how early they block, then place each beside the claim that creates it.

rules.name: Proof shows the mechanism
rules.check: When the brief supplies no proof asset for a claim, the proof zone renders a schema-faithful depiction of the product mechanism built only from supplied fields, flows, or records, rather than prose alone.
rules.fix: Draw the mechanism from supplied facts — the template, the flow, the record — and place it as the claim's evidence; add nothing the facts do not supply.

rules.name: Every section carries a belief delta
rules.check: Each section names the belief before it and the stronger belief after it, and survives the removal, objection, and unique-evidence tests.
rules.fix: Delete, merge, or rewrite sections that produce no belief delta.

rules.name: Pricing exposes the real decision
rules.check: Comparison leads with the criteria that change plan choice and states total cost drivers, limits, renewal, and cancellation terms in plain language.
rules.fix: Surface the deciding criteria and mandatory costs; remove decoy plans and unevidenced popularity marks.

rules.name: Mode declared before form
rules.check: One mode is named in the design contract before layout, components, tone, or motion are chosen.
rules.fix: State the human goal as a verb and write the mode into the contract.

rules.name: Mode purity
rules.check: One success signal governs the whole surface; a second human goal lives on another surface, step, or clearly bounded region.
rules.fix: Choose the dominant mode and split the competing goal out. Name the defect Mode Collision.

rules.name: Density matches frequency and expertise
rules.check: Density follows use frequency, expertise, and consequence rather than a default low-density template.
rules.fix: Raise density for frequent expert use and lower it for rare or first-time use.

rules.name: Action posture matches the mode
rules.check: The action posture is the one the declared mode prescribes: one commitment for persuade, scoped and reversible for operate, interpretation before action for analyze, quiet and contextual for read, invitational for experience.
rules.fix: Restyle or relocate actions to the posture the declared mode prescribes.

rules.name: Motion budget matches the mode
rules.check: Motion spends only the budget the mode earns: low for operate and read, medium for persuade and analyze, high only where motion is authored into the work.
rules.fix: Remove motion the declared mode does not earn.

rules.name: Characteristic failure absent
rules.check: The declared mode's characteristic failure is absent: Promise Parade, Action Flatland, Chart Dump, Content Fog, or Interface Eclipse.
rules.fix: Name the failure present and rebuild the offending zone against the mode's commit list.

rules.name: Mode detected from the human verb
rules.check: Where the brief declares no mode, the mode follows the strongest consequential verb and the observable finish, not the artifact noun.
rules.fix: Extract the human, verb, consequence, and finish; state one assumption, or ask when two outcomes carry equal consequence.

rules.name: Current idea outranks chrome
rules.check: P0 is the current proposition, instruction, or answer, not the page title, navigation, or table of contents.
rules.fix: Demote chrome to P4 and give the current idea the focal position.

rules.name: Headings do argumentative work
rules.check: Every heading advances the argument instead of labeling a container, and card grids do not fragment a line of thought.
rules.fix: Rewrite each heading as the claim, question, or step it introduces.

rules.name: Stable measure and explicit location
rules.check: Reading measure, semantic heading order, visible focus, readable contrast, and an explicit location in long content are preserved.
rules.fix: Restore the measure and heading order, and add a persistent location indicator.

rules.name: Definitions at the point of need
rules.check: Definitions, examples, and references are reachable where comprehension needs them, without losing the reading position.
rules.fix: Move the definition inline or into an adjacent reveal at first use.

rules.name: No invented sources or certainty
rules.check: Citations, results, endorsements, and stated certainty are real.
rules.fix: Cite the real source, or state the uncertainty plainly.

rules.name: Long-content states specified
rules.check: Loading, missing sources, outdated guidance, permission-limited sections, broken references, print, copy, and narrow-width reflow behavior are specified.
rules.fix: Specify each of those states before compose.

rules.name: The work holds the focal position
rules.check: P0 is the work or the moment it appoints, never a logo, navigation bar, or explanatory frame.
rules.fix: Demote chrome to P4 and give the work visual command.

rules.name: Motion is authored, not decorative
rules.check: Every transition carries a narrative or perceptual role, and stillness is used as a deliberate choice.
rules.fix: Cut transitions that carry no role in the direction.

rules.name: Controls stay operable under immersion
rules.check: Keyboard operation, visible focus, captions or transcripts where applicable, reduced-motion behavior, and mute or pause control for playable media are present, and no safety or consent control is hidden.
rules.fix: Restore the missing control. Immersion never justifies removing it.

rules.name: Fallback preserves the encounter
rules.check: Unsupported media, constrained devices, and reduced-motion paths present a stable fallback that preserves the intended meaning.
rules.fix: Author the fallback as part of the direction rather than leaving a degraded remainder.

rules.name: Point of view over spectacle
rules.check: Composition, sound, interaction, and transition carry one stated point of view rather than substituting effect for it.
rules.fix: State the point of view and cut what does not carry it.

rules.name: No competing task on the surface
rules.check: Concurrent commerce, administration, or reference tasks live on another surface rather than interrupting the authored sequence.
rules.fix: Move the competing task off the surface and link to it.

rules.name: Rendered claims trace to supplied facts
rules.check: Every material claim in rendered copy, visible or assistive — a policy, capability, commitment, prior condition, metric definition, quantity, duration, or data fact — traces to the brief, the target source, or user-supplied evidence.
rules.fix: Delete the claim, reword it to what the supplied facts support, or record the gap as a FRAME.md assumption that never renders.

rules.name: Unsupplied policy never renders as product fact
rules.check: No rendered copy asserts an account, permission, reversibility, retention, enforcement, or delivery policy the facts do not supply; unsupplied policies are recorded as assumptions and designed conservatively without being stated.
rules.fix: Move the policy to FRAME.md as an assumption, design the conservative behavior, and strip the assertion from the copy.

rules.name: Sample data instantiates, never asserts
rules.check: Illustrative records fill only the supplied schema and stay consistent with supplied figures; no rendered total, distribution, trend, availability statement, or contact detail extends the supplied facts.
rules.fix: Derive every figure from a supplied one, drop unsupplied attributes, render unset state for current values the facts do not supply, and mark instance data as illustrative in the artifact record.

rules.name: Outcome copy states what the system verifiably did
rules.check: Success and confirmation copy asserts only outcomes the built mechanism actually produces; no claimed delivery, response, follow-up, or restoration without a supplied mechanism.
rules.fix: Reword to the verifiable event and remove promised outcomes no supplied mechanism backs.

rules.name: Assistive text never outruns visible copy
rules.check: No aria-label, alt text, or visually hidden summary asserts a fact stronger or more specific than the visible copy supports.
rules.fix: Rewrite assistive text as a restatement of visible, supported content.

rules.name: The chain never renders
rules.check: No rendered copy exposes the design's own reasoning or the brief's instructions to the builder — no ranking rationale, no completeness meta-claims about the page itself, no restated constraints; internal reasoning lives in the artifact record only.
rules.fix: Move the rationale to the artifact record and delete it from the copy; a builder constraint is never a product fact.

rules.name: Operate chrome stays quiet
rules.check: On operate-mode surfaces, navigation, headers, and section chrome stay near-monochrome and low-contrast; the palette expresses itself in data color, status, and the primary action, not in filled navigation or display-scale headings.
rules.fix: Strip fills and emphasis from chrome, demote heading scale, and reserve the direction's palette for data, status, and the primary action.

rules.name: Controls carry their consequences
rules.check: Every setting or consequential control carries a point-of-need description drawn from supplied facts, and any gating (plan, permission, prerequisite) is cued on the control rather than discovered on failure.
rules.fix: Add a one-line supplied-fact description per control and surface the gating cue beside it; never invent the consequence (HON-02).

rules.name: Action color matches the emotional target
rules.check: Primary actions and ambient chrome avoid alarm-coded hues on every surface unless the action is destructive or the surface's job is to warn; on surfaces whose job is calming or focus this extends to accents, and when the dealt direction's accent conflicts with the surface's emotional target or with the action's meaning, the accent is re-mapped rather than applied verbatim.
rules.fix: Reserve alarm hues for destructive or warning actions; choose a calm-coded or neutral-coded accent consistent with the direction for every other primary action.

rules.name: Retrieval genre outranks the direction
rules.check: Documentation and reference surfaces keep genre conventions — neutral high-contrast ground, persistent identity and navigation, density tuned for scanning — with the dealt direction expressed in accents and details rather than a re-theme.
rules.fix: Restore neutral ground, persistent navigation and page identity, and scannable density; confine the direction to accents.

rules.name: The direction serves the genre
rules.check: On trust- or genre-governed surfaces (auth, payment, pricing, documentation, daily-operate tools), genre conventions own ground color, chrome, input affordances, and color semantics; the dealt direction expresses itself in accents, type details, and structure rather than as a costume.
rules.fix: Restore the genre's conventions and re-map the direction into accents and details; adapting the direction to the genre is required fidelity, not a re-roll.

rules.name: The direction survives the register
rules.check: When a house style or brand register is supplied as fact, the dealt direction still gets at least one unmistakable, considered expression inside that register — a signature structural move, a deliberate density rhythm, a scale contrast; a build whose only register-compliant answer is the default component set reads as a template.
rules.fix: Find the degrees of freedom the register leaves open and spend the direction there; never spend it by breaking the supplied register, and never spend it nowhere.

rules.name: The price is the P0 value
rules.check: On a pricing surface, price carries value-weight above its labels, and every choosable tier renders a reachable action.
rules.fix: Apply label-value inversion to the price and give each tier a working commitment path.

rules.name: Visual products get visual evidence
rules.check: When the offer is a physical or visual object, the page develops its visual evidence within the supplied facts — the supplied depiction rendered at more than one honest view (full object, meaningful detail, in-context scale, per-variant state) — rather than a single lone rendering; missing photography is a constraint to design around, not a void to leave.
rules.fix: Render the supplied geometry or spec at several honest views; generic context (a wall, a hand, a room) is instantiation, invented product attributes are not.

rules.name: The argument survives collapse
rules.check: At rest — before any hover, expansion, or navigation — each offered case or item presents its claim plus at least one decisive supplied evidence element (scope, constraint, outcome, metric, or mechanism); collapse and disclosure defer depth, never the case itself, and a block showing only a name and kicker asks for the click on faith.
rules.fix: Lift the evidence spine into the resting block and move only elaboration behind disclosure; if the facts supply scope, constraint, and outcome, the resting card carries them.

rules.name: Whole before large
rules.check: A reproduced work (poster, screen, print, artwork supplied as evidence) is shown whole — uncropped, its title or wordmark fully legible — within the first viewport before any at-scale, zoomed, or cropped view; a text column paired with an artifact either matches the artifact's height or the artifact is sized to the column, so no viewport shows a cut-off artifact beside a void.
rules.fix: Lead with the complete artifact at a size that fits the viewport, offer scale as a second view, and size the paired column and artifact to the same bounds.

rules.name: The offer set is visible before the argument
rules.check: On a pricing or plan-selection surface every offered plan's name and price is visible in the first viewport, whatever framing the dealt hand supplies; an objection, calculation, or story that precedes the offer set organises around it, never above it, so a visitor who has not chosen a tier can scan the options without scrolling.
rules.fix: Place the plan set (names and prices at minimum) in the first viewport and let the framing sit beside or beneath it; keep the full comparison below.

rules.name: Inputs look like inputs
rules.check: Text inputs render a visible boundary or fill, a visible focus state, and a tap target findable by eye; underline-only fields are not used on mobile forms.
rules.fix: Give inputs a bounded or filled treatment with a visible focus state sized for touch.

rules.name: One ask per mobile step
rules.check: On mobile flows each step carries one primary ask; credential pairs and multi-field steps are split rather than stacked on small screens.
rules.fix: Split the step; more, lighter steps beat one heavy step on a small screen.

rules.name: No step is a dead end
rules.check: Every flow step renders a visible way back or out, and back honors the preservation the flow promises.
rules.fix: Add the back or close affordance and state what leaving or returning preserves.

rules.name: Adjacent tiers separate decisively
rules.check: Adjacent hierarchy tiers differ in at least two of size step, weight, or spatial treatment, by enough to distinguish at a glance; same-size same-weight tiers, or a distinction carried only by Regular versus Medium, are one tier rendered twice.
rules.fix: Move each tier a full scale step apart in two dimensions or merge the tiers; hierarchy that needs inspection to perceive is not hierarchy.

rules.name: The polish pass
rules.check: A final zoomed pass confirms every spacing and size value sits on the scale, same-role elements are styled identically everywhere, all-caps labels carry opened tracking, display copy has no widowed last word, and the squint test still resolves primary, secondary, and groupings.
rules.fix: Fix the drift, re-run the squint test, and re-verify the proximity ratio (HIER-07) and rhythm limit (COMP-18) survived late edits.
